Previously a plastics engineer, he built his fortune through the chain's flotation and sale to Electronics Boutique. Family and venture-capital funding helped the young retailer expand before Taylor became an investor in other businesses.

long_biography.plain_text:
The TeamSport management buyout brought investor Neil Taylor together with Connection Capital to finance the karting operator's expansion. Their investment accompanied bank debt, giving the management team resources to develop new tracks and acquire existing venues. The plan targeted a fragmented market in which many small operators lacked continuing investment.

Taylor's family office also owned an engineering business with operations in Britain and the United States. He worked with consultant Colin Hurren on its reorganisation, following an examination of the company's recent difficulties. Taylor valued the calm handling of a sensitive process, describing the resulting restructuring as successful.

confidence.reason: Primary lender release specifies the investors, separate debt and expansion mechanism; Taylor’s own testimonial supports his participation and stated assessment of restructuring.
